cells.tense: You are already weighing what's fair, and the scale moves easily.
cells.ask: End one arrangement you've kept past its usefulness, and say plainly what it was.
cells.core:
You read what's fair without doing sums about it. Someone takes a little more and you feel it; someone takes less and you notice that too. Then it goes into the shape of things — how the work runs, how people split what's there — and it holds. That's the groundedness most people are chasing and rarely reach.

The next thing this can feed is an ending. Something in the structure you set is finished, and keeping it upright costs more than it returns. You don't have to accuse anyone or relitigate it. Just say what it was and let it stop.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel what's fair and give it its shape.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed and giving it its fair measure
cells.place: where patterns get set and the structure holds

cells.tense: You will be ready with the tally long before the moment arrives.
cells.ask: Let one debt stay unsettled for a week without mentioning or tracking it.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead there's a moment where the account gets squared, and you're already keeping it. Who took credit, who left early, who owes what — the running total stays with you, and it costs you like a second job. What was supposed to make things workable has turned into a ledger you carry alone.

There's a steadier version where your endurance is what keeps the thing standing rather than what keeps score. Try it small. Let one thing you're owed sit unsaid this week. Not forgiven, not surrendered — just not collected yet. See what it's like to hold it without the arithmetic.
cells.sheetLine: The structure has turned into a ledger you keep alone.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed and giving it its fair measure

cells.tense: You were shown once that asking for your share goes badly.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're owed, to one person, and let their answer stand as it is.
cells.core:
You can see what's fair as clearly as anyone. In a good week that reads as patience — you let a small slight pass, you keep the room calm, you don't make everything a fight. That gift is real. Where it bends is the claim. You leave your share unasked rather than risk the trouble, so someone else's slice keeps coming out bigger and you go along.

The missing move is from seeing it to saying it. Start small. One thing you're owed, named to one person, out loud. They might disagree. The point isn't the verdict. It's that the pattern you keep together can survive a sentence about what you want.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's fair and you don't say it.

cells.tense: You are tallying grievances against a ledger you didn't agree to keep.
cells.ask: Say one thing you've been counting, in plain words, to the person it's about.
cells.core:
Fairness is running in you right now, quietly. You notice when something's off — a slight, an imbalance, a favor not returned — and you adjust for it without announcing it. In its good shape that's a fine read on a room — you feel the tilt early and correct for it before anyone else has looked up. Where it bends is the secrecy. Little weights, old ones mostly, still sitting on the scale, and when a situation tips further than it should you can't say why it bothers you.

One of those weights has been there longest. You don't need the argument that justifies it. Say it out loud, plainly, once, and see what comes back.
cells.sheetLine: You've been keeping a tally you didn't say you were keeping.
cells.verb: weighing what's owed and giving it its fair measure
